trap and fail propagate outward through every construct (they are not caught by catch: catch handles only declared errors and none; a trap always keeps the state).

  • E1 Fuel exhaustion is uncatchable. Running out of fuel is not a declared error and not a trap a program can observe: no catch, try or try e else X handles it, it propagates outward through every construct, and it keeps the state exactly as a trap does (T8). The derivation: if a handler could observe exhaustion, a program could return a different value on a larger budget, and a completed result would depend on fuel. The fuel laws require that it does not: more fuel never changes a completed result (RCE.Core.eval_mono, eval_fuel_indep in lean/RCE/Core/Fuel.lean). A conforming run of (e catch |x| h) where e exhausts its fuel ends in exhaustion, never in h.

&mut write-back (normative). A call that returns writes back each &mut argument and a &mut self receiver. A call that ends by fail leaves each of them as it was at the call, provided every effect since entry is undoable, and requires change otherwise (F.4.4, W-TX-1); the callee's writes made before the failure are undone. Atomicity of the event is separate: a trap, or a fail that leaves the step, keeps the state: the state is the pre-state (T8). The earlier rule of this text wrote back on every outcome, including fail; it is retired because F.4.4 makes a failed call a no-op, which is what a caller can reason about. T33 now proves the restore rule (WriteBack.t33_failure_restores, t33_return_writes_back); nothing about the retired rule remains in the proved tree. The program emitters implement the rule for a write-back call that is a whole statement or expression of a let, var, assignment, emit or return, and for such a call under catch or try (f(&mut x) catch h, try f(&mut x)): the call is the first thing the statement evaluates, so it can be hoisted without changing evaluation order or budget charges. A write-back call nested deeper in a strict position (an operand of an operator, an argument, a list or map element, a receiver) is first rewritten by one shared A-normal-form pass that runs before all three emitters (spec/checker/src/anf.rs): the operands evaluated before it are bound to fresh let temporaries in left-to-right order, then the call, so reads, budget charges and emits keep their order (T34). A write-back call in a conditional position (right of and/or, an if branch, a catch handler, a lambda or a comprehension) is not flattened, since that would evaluate it eagerly; it requires change, with a diagnostic, and is never given a different meaning. Tested on every target (spec/checker/tests/write_back.rs). Values of type τ ! ε are val(v) or err(X, v); they are first-class only until a try or catch consumes them.

sections.title: 6.3 Edge semantics of primitives (normative, from form/num.rs)
sections.html:
These are the Form's own rules; every implementation reproduces them exactly.

  • N1 Numbers. A Form number is an int (i64, or u64 per N2) or a float (finite f64). The type is part of the value and is kept across every boundary: a float with no fractional part stays a float (10.0 is written 10.0 in canonical JSON, 10 is an int), and -0.0 keeps its sign (N3 F6). Derivation: encoding must be injective and round-trip, decode(encode(v)) == v, because replay rebuilds state from D. Turning 10.0 into 10 at a boundary would decode as an int, changing the static type a later step sees and the bits of later float arithmetic, so no normalization is applied. RCE's static types make the int/float distinction visible to the programmer, and canonical JSON keeps it visible in D.
  • N2 Integer arithmetic is checked: overflow of the static type's range is trap("overflow: V is outside T") with V the exact result and T the static type (i64 for an untyped literal), never a wrap. / truncates toward zero (-7 / 2 = -3); % has the sign of the dividend (-3 % 2 = -1). Division or remainder by zero is trap("division by zero"). Modular and clamped arithmetic are explicit methods, never the default: a.wrapping_add(b), wrapping_sub, wrapping_mul give the result modulo 2^N mapped into the static type's range, and saturating_add, saturating_sub, saturating_mul clamp it to the range; neither traps. u64 and usize arithmetic uses the Form ops uadd usub umul udiv urem (draft 0.5), which compute the exact result and trap unless it lies in [0, 2^64); a value at or above 2^63 is carried as an unsigned Form int, so 18446744073709551615 - 1 is exact. Lean: RCE/U64.lean. i64.MIN / -1 and i64.MIN % -1 are trap("overflow: 9223372036854775808 is outside i64") (the quotient is out of range; Rust's checked_rem). Shifts: x << n and x >> n with n ≥ bit width or n < 0 are trap("shift amount out of range"); >> is arithmetic for signed and logical for unsigned types. Bitwise & | ^ ~ act on the two's-complement representation of the static type.
  • N3 Floats. The rules below are derived from IEEE 754-2019 and from two requirements of the Form: replay must give the same bits on every target (T1), and δ must be total (S1). tests/float_rules.rs checks each rule on the interpreter; the parity set carries the vectors of examples/57_float_vectors.rce to every CI target.
    • F1 Correct rounding. f64 is IEEE binary64. + - * / and sqrt are the standard's basic operations, correctly rounded with roundTiesToEven, the default rounding-direction attribute; so are the conversion of an integer (as f64) and of a decimal literal. A correctly rounded operation is a function of its operands' bits alone, so every conforming target gives the same result: this is the only property determinism needs, and no other rounding mode exists in RCE.
    • F2 One rounding per operator, in source order. Float addition and multiplication are not associative and a * b + c with one rounding differs from two roundings (vector MulSub: 0.1 * 10.0 - 1.0 is 0, fused it is 5.551115123125783e-17). Contraction to fused multiply-add, reassociation, excess precision and every other value-changing optimization the standard allows a language to permit are therefore not valid compilations (HC-14). A fused multiply-add is itself correctly rounded, so it may exist only as an explicit named operation; RCE has none yet. Adding one needs a correctly rounded implementation on every runtime (Rust f64::mul_add, Java Math.fma, exact rational rounding in Python and JavaScript).
    • F3 Subnormals are preserved. Gradual underflow is part of the binary64 format; flush-to-zero and denormals-are-zero modes are not IEEE operations and would make x - y == 0 hold for x != y. A host never enables them (HC-13); vectors Mul(5e-324, 3.0) and Mul(2.2250738585072014e-308, 0.5) detect either mode.
    • F4 Non-finite results trap (from totality). A Form value must have a reflexive equality and a total order (6.2, N5, N6) and must encode as a JSON number for hashing (N1). NaN is unequal to itself under IEEE comparison, and an infinity is not a JSON number and reintroduces NaN through inf - inf and 0 * inf; the largest subset of binary64 closed under these requirements is the finite values. δ is total as a function into values and traps, so an operation whose IEEE result is not finite (the standard's overflow, divideByZero and invalid exceptions) is trap("non-finite float"). The alternatives fail a law: admitting NaN under the standard's totalOrder makes == disagree with IEEE comparison and needs a canonical NaN for hashing; saturating to the largest finite value is not an IEEE result and breaks x * 2.0 / 2.0 == x without a signal. With the trap every value is finite and every result that does not trap is the IEEE result. x / 0.0 and sqrt of a negative number trap.
    • F5 NaN payloads are never observable. By F4 no NaN becomes a value, so its sign, payload and quiet bit cannot reach state, output or a hash; the standard leaves payload propagation to the implementation, which is why this matters. An implementation tests for a non-finite result before any NaN escapes, and the trap text is the same for every NaN. A fabric or target that can produce NaN (GPU, NPU, WASM SIMD) canonicalizes or traps before a value reaches state (HC-13; wasm_float.rs rewrites NaN to the canonical positive NaN).
    • F6 Signed zero is a distinct state. -0.0 arises by the standard's sign rules, which are exact, so every target produces it in the same places (vector Mul(0.0, -1.0)). It is observable: tostr prints -0 (f64 and f32 alike, so text round-trips), and the sign decides later results through the same exact rules. The state hash must be injective on observable state, so canonical JSON keeps the sign and a state holding -0.0 hashes differently from one holding 0.0; the canonical order (6.1) is totalOrder, so they are distinct map keys. -0.0 == 0.0 is still true: == is IEEE comparison.
    • F7 Exception flags are not state. Inexact and underflow raise nothing (F1 already fixes the result); overflow, divideByZero and invalid are the trap of F4. No program reads a flag.
    • F8 Exact operations. floor, ceil and round are the standard's roundToIntegral operations toward negative, toward positive and ties-away ((2.5).round() is 3, (-2.5).round() is -3); abs clears the sign. min and max follow N5. None of these rounds.
    • F9 Transcendentals are correctly rounded RCE code, or absent. IEEE 754-2019 recommends but does not require correctly rounded exp, log, sin, pow and the like, and platform math libraries differ in the last bit, so no runtime takes one from its platform library and no Form op names one. A transcendental exists only as RCE source in the standard library module math (stdlib/lib/math/math.rce), built from the operations of F1 to F8 and integers, so every runtime carries the same algorithm and the result is the same bits on every target (vector parity: Rust, Python, JavaScript, Scala). Each function must be correctly rounded by construction: algebraic ones (cbrt, hypot) compare the exact value with the rounding midpoints in exact arithmetic (TwoSum, Veltkamp/Dekker TwoProduct, Shewchuk expansions; exact ties round to even); transcendental ones use Ziv's strategy over exact integers (the value is bracketed with an explicit error bound and the precision grows until both ends round alike; a transcendental value of a double is never a midpoint), sin and cos with Payne-Hanek reduction exact for every finite argument. Each is checked bit for bit against MPFR on the CORE-MATH worst cases. Present: sqrt (F1), cbrt, hypot, exp, log, log2, log10, sin, cos; any other (pow, tan, atan2, ...) is absent until it meets the same rule. A result that overflows traps (F4); log of x ≤ 0 traps (also log2, log10). Device versions stay output only or verified (HC-13). Float text (the result of tostr and of Show on a float, interp::float_text) is the shortest round-trip digits; decimal notation for 1e-5 ≤ |x| < 1e16, else d.ddde±N with + on positive exponents (1e+300, 1.5e-7). It is a program-visible value and is never hashed. Canonical JSON (6.1.1) is a different, separately specified byte form: it has one float form, interp::float_json, used for hashes and for every trace and log written as JSON, so a trace shows the bytes that were hashed: shortest round-trip digits, decimal with at least one fractional digit for 1e-4 ≤ |x| < 1e16 (10.0, 0.0001), otherwise exponent form without + (1e16, 1e-5, 5e-324), and -0.0 keeps its sign (tests/traces.rs pins these forms). f32 (draft 0.5). The Form ops f32add f32sub f32mul f32div round both operands to binary32, compute in binary64, and round the result to binary32 (round to nearest even). Binary64 has 53 ≥ 2·24 + 2 significand bits, so by Figueroa's theorem the result equals the correctly rounded binary32 result, and every target (Rust f32, Python struct, JavaScript Math.fround) gives the same bits. A result outside the binary32 range is trap("non-finite float"). x as f32 (Form tof32) rounds once. Lean: RCE/F32.lean.
  • N4 Mixed arithmetic does not exist in RCE (both operands of a binary operator have the same static type). a as f64 converts an integer exactly when |a| ≤ 2^53 and otherwise rounds to nearest even; x as iN truncates toward zero and traps if the result is out of range or x is not finite.
  • N5 min / max compare exactly on integers and by IEEE order on floats (total, since operands are finite); on a tie the receiver is returned.
  • N6 Equality is structural value equality within one static type; 1 == 1.0 is a type error (the type is part of the value, N1). Float == is IEEE comparison, so -0.0 == 0.0 although the two are distinct states (N3 F6).
  • N7 Text is a sequence of Unicode scalar values compared by code point, stored as UTF-8. From draft 0.5, len, indexing and slicing count UTF-8 bytes (Form blen, bget, bslice): s[i] is a u8, and a slice whose ends are not character boundaries is trap("not a char boundary"). for c in s and chars() still go by character. Case mapping (upper, lower) and class tests (isdigit, isalpha, isupper, islower) are ASCII-only; other characters are unchanged / false. strip, words and toint treat as whitespace exactly the 25 code points of the White_Space property of Unicode 18.0.0: U+0009 to U+000D, U+0020, U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000 to U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F and U+3000 (interp::WHITE_SPACE). isspace is ASCII (space, \t, \n, \x0c, \r). Display writes text in double quotes, with U+0000, tab, LF, CR, " and \ as \0, \t, \n, \r, \" and \\, each code point of the display escape set as \u{h} (h its lower-case hexadecimal digits, without leading zeros), and every other code point as itself. The display escape set is the 911 ranges of code points listed in spec/data/display-escape.json (interp::display_escaped; the emitter writes the same ranges into each emitted runtime): the control characters, the code points that are not printable and the grapheme extenders, as Rust 1.98.1 escapes them in the Debug form of a string from its tables of Unicode 17.0.0, enumerated once. The file, not a Unicode version, defines the set. Unicode pin. RCE pins Unicode 18.0.0 (https://www.unicode.org/versions/Unicode18.0.0/) and reads no Unicode table at run time: scalar values and UTF-8 do not change between versions, case and class operations are ASCII, and the two sets of code points a result depends on, White_Space and the display escape set, are enumerated above rather than taken from the toolchain. A newer Rust, Python, JavaScript or JVM therefore cannot change a result; tests/unicode_pin.rs checks both sets and scans the runtimes for calls that would read the toolchain's tables, {:?} of a text among them, and tests/emit.rs compares the display of both ends of every range, and of the code points beside them, on each emitted target with the reference. Moving the pin is a spec change that must leave the enumerated sets unchanged or bump the draft.
  • N8 Indexing The index i of a[i] and the ends of a[i:j] have type usize (W-TY-1 otherwise), so no index is negative. a[i] with i ≥ n is trap("index i out of range"). A slice end above n is trap("slice index out of range"), and i > j is trap("slice bounds reversed"); an omitted end is 0 or n. Indexing and slicing are total or trapping by one rule: an out-of-range position is never silently moved.
  • N9 Limits. A list or text built by any operation is at most SIZE_LIMIT = 1,000,000 elements (trap("size limit")). A value written to state is at most VALUE_LIMIT = 1,048,576 bytes of canonical JSON (trap("value limit"), the state is kept, the value is not recorded).
  • N10 Absence. none and a present () differ, exactly as the Form's null-versus-absent rule: an option field holding none is present.
  • N11 Time is the logical clock only: Tick events and after n in select. No construct reads a wall clock.

The built-in methods are exactly the table of 5.15 (the closed standard library); each has the semantics of the Form primitive of the same name in num.rs and ir.rs (Prim, Map, Filter, Fold, SortBy), at the RCE static type. A Form primitive that is not in that table (for example pow, floordiv, pmod, zip, replace, unique) is not an RCE method and is W-NAME-1. sort and sort_by are stable.

chapters.title: 6 (continued). Dynamic semantics: steps, loops and concurrency
chapters.question: Name-free hashing uses indices named after which logician? (two words)

sections.html: This section defines the step function δ (delta), which takes a state and an event and returns the next state and an outcome, then errors, hashing, loop bounds, concurrency and how examples are checked. A trap is a defined failure after which the event does not apply and the state is kept. Example: a loop with bound 10 that starts an 11th iteration traps with "loop bound".

sections.title: 6.4 The step function δ
sections.html:
For event e = (Eₗ, v):

  1. For each region Rᵢ in declaration order, take the steps step Rᵢ on p if g in source order whose pattern p matches e and whose guard g evaluates to true in (Rᵢ's pre-state fields, bindings of p). The first such step is the step of Rᵢ for e. If there is none, Rᵢ is unchanged (frame). A guard that traps (overflow, division by zero, …) does not fall through to the next step: the state is kept, with that trap (change S1; this is what makes δ a total function rather than leaving the case undefined).
  2. Every selected step runs on the pre-state s (ASM semantics, Form law 2): no step sees another region's update for the same event.
  3. The body of the step of Rᵢ is evaluated with fields of Rᵢ bound as vars to rᵢ, the pattern bindings as lets. Its result is
    • ok(σ′): rᵢ′ = the field values in σ′ (each checked against its type range and VALUE_LIMIT), outputs oᵢ = the values emitted, in order;
    • fail(X, w) or trap(m): the step is kept.
  4. If any selected step is kept, the whole event does not apply: δ(s, e) = (s, [Kept(X or trap(m), e)]), where X is the reason of the first kept region in declaration order. Atomicity: an event either applies to every region or to none.
  5. Otherwise δ(s, e) = ((r₁′, …, rₖ′), o₁ ++ … ++ oₖ).

The arrow form step R on p -> e is sugar for the block f = e where f is R's only field.

Order independence. Since each step reads only its own region and the event, the result of steps 2–5 does not depend on the order regions are evaluated except through "first kept region", which is fixed by declaration order. Outputs are concatenated in declaration order.

sections.title: 6.5 Errors, traps and kept steps
sections.html: A fail X(…) or a trap inside a step keeps the state: the state is unchanged, the log records the event with outcome kept(X) and λ outputs Kept. Nothing is thrown past a step; no event is dropped silently. In a pure function called from comptime, a trap or fail is a compile error. In main, a trap or unhandled failure ends the run stopped, with the trap or failure as its output.

sections.title: 6.6 Determinism of identity: name-free hashing
sections.html:
Channel ids, actor ids and task ids are not counters. A channel id is the SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of (creating construct's name-free key, creating task id, per-task creation index), where the name-free key replaces identifiers by their De Bruijn position (Form law 2). An actor id and a task id are stable paths (C.11.11): an actor is keyed by its supervision position i.j (supervisor i in declaration order, its child j) or - when no supervisor declares its type, the creating task id, and its ordinal among that task's creations at that position; a task by its parent's id and its ordinal among the parent's spawns; fn main is the root. No key contains an identifier, so renaming every identifier in a program leaves every id, every log hash and every select decision unchanged (T7); no actor or task key contains a source position, so an edit that keeps the supervision tree and the order of creations keeps every actor and task id.

The concept record (informative). Names carry no meaning in the Form (T7) and most of the meaning for a reader: obscuring identifiers costs a model between a tenth and a quarter of its accuracy on what a program does (arXiv 2510.03178, 2025), while removing formatting costs nothing measurable (arXiv 2508.13666, 2025; both in section 11). So names have a defined home outside the hash. The concept record of a module is the table from each name-free key of 6.6 to: the name as written, the intent strings of the item, and its doc comments. rce emit form prints it under a names field after the hashed fields, keyed #i by declaration index (the same index shape_ctl of 6.10 uses), with the intent strings; doc comments are not yet collected. The Form JSON of 10.5 still carries names in its name and region fields. It is never read by δ. Two modules that differ only in it have the same outcomes, outputs, ids and log hashes (6.1 hashes the positional forms, T7; the finding of 2026-10-22 that the hashes covered names is resolved, see C.15). A projection (10.5) renders the concept record's names by default; rce fmt nameless (10.6) is the projection that renders positional names instead, which is the text the name-free keys of 6.6 are computed from.

sections.title: 6.7 Loops and fuel
sections.html:
for p in e iterates over a finite value (list, set, map in canonical order of its keys, as in 7.1, never insertion order (an erratum, C.15), text by scalar value, or an integer range a..b / a..=b); its length is fixed when the loop starts, and mutating the iterated collection inside the loop requires change statically (it is borrowed). while c bound n and loop bound n run at most n iterations, n a comptime-or-runtime u64 evaluated once; the default bound is LOOP_LIMIT = 1,000,000. A program may set its own default with a module-level const LOOP_LIMIT: u64 = n, n a positive literal (draft 0.5; any other declaration of that name requires change, W-LOOP-1). Starting iteration n + 1 is trap("loop bound"). Comptime evaluation uses the same bounds. for x in f(…) over an iterator function (5.14) counts yields against LOOP_LIMIT in the same way; Lean: RCE/Iter.lean (drive_total, drive_break).

Structural recursion (draft 0.4). A function may call itself when every self-call passes, in one parameter position i fixed for the function, a name bound inside a constructor pattern of a match whose scrutinee is parameter i (or a name already known to be such a component). The argument is then a strict component of the value received, so along any chain of calls the value at position i strictly shrinks and the depth of recursion is at most the number of constructor nodes in that value, which N9 bounds. A name that is rebound by let, var, assignment or a for pattern loses this status. The checkers of drafts 0.4 to 0.7 let the position differ from call to call; that admits a function that never returns (f(x, y) whose one self-call takes a component of x and a fixed value for y, and whose other takes a fixed value for x and a component of y, runs forever from f(Leaf, Node(…))), so such a function requires change (W-REC-1; an erratum, C.15). Every function this paragraph admits is admitted by the rule below with one layer.

Recursion by layered measures. Every cycle of the call graph (a strongly connected component: one function that calls itself, or two or more functions; trait methods excluded) is admitted when its calls can be done in layers. A layer gives each function f of the cycle a set P f of parameter positions and the summed measure μ_f(ā) = Σ_{i ∈ P f} size(aᵢ), with size the number of constructor nodes. A call g(b̄) written in f keeps the measure when the positions P g map one to one into P f so that the argument at each j ∈ P g is the parameter at its image i (unchanged, the name not rebound) or a component of it in the sense of structural recursion above; it shrinks the measure when at least one of them is a component. Layer 1 must be kept by every call of the cycle and shrunk by at least one; the calls it shrinks are done. Layer 2 must be kept by every call not yet done and shrunk by at least one of them, and so on. The cycle is admitted when the calls left after some layer k form no cycle among the functions. Then the tuple (μ₁, …, μ_k, rank of the function) falls lexicographically at every call: a call done at layer j keeps μ₁ … μ_{j−1} and shrinks μ_j, and a call left over keeps every μ and lowers the rank. The order is well founded, so every chain of calls is finite; with one layer a chain inside the cycle has at most (μ + 1)·k calls, with μ the measure of the first call and k the number of functions in the cycle, and N9 bounds μ. The reference checker tries every choice of the sets of a layer, in a fixed order, for a cycle with at most 16 parameters in total, takes the first choice that does the most calls, and reports that a larger cycle that needs a layer requires change. Lean: RCE/Mutual.lean (call_dec, call_keep, layer_dec, wf_total, wf_fuel_irrelevant; one layer: lex_dec, mutual_total, mutual_fuel_irrelevant, mutual_depth). Examples: even(xs) and odd(xs) that each call the other on the tail of a matched Cons (one layer); h(m, n) that calls h(m', n) and h(m, n') on components m' of m and n' of n (layer {m} does the first call, layer {n} the second).

Declared bounds. fn f(…) -> τ bound n, n a positive integer literal, allows at most n active calls of f at once: a call of f, once its arguments are evaluated and fitted to the parameter types, traps with trap("recursion bound") when n calls of f are already active, and otherwise counts as active until it returns or fails. A cycle that no layers admit is admitted when every cycle of calls inside it passes through a function declared with bound (the calls between functions without one form no cycle). Then the slack Σ (n_g − active calls of g) over the bounded functions falls at every call of a bounded function and the rank falls at every other call, so every run of the cycle ends, by its value or by the trap, within (slack + 1)·k nested calls. This covers recursion on integers or indices, which has no constructor measure (gcd(a, b) calling gcd(b, a % b), a parser that recurses on a position). The counts belong to the task (6.8) that makes the calls, so par and for … par inside a function of a cycle with a bounded function require change (W-REC-1): the branches could otherwise count calls differently on one thread and on several. bound on an iterator function (5.14), a foreign function or a trait signature is W-REC-1. The check costs nothing (C.6.4 is unchanged). Lean: RCE/Mutual.lean (bump_slack, bound_dec, with lex_dec, mutual_total, mutual_depth); tests: spec/checker/tests/bound.rs.

Any other cycle in the call graph requires change (W-REC-1).

This is what makes δ total (T2): every construct terminates in a number of steps bounded by a function of the program and the event.

sections.title: 6.8 Concurrency: tasks, channels, select, actors
sections.html:
Concurrency is defined by a small-step semantics over configurations C = (T, K, A, L): a finite map T of tasks (id ↦ continuation), channels K (id ↦ capacity, FIFO buffer, closed flag, held-send queue), actors A (id ↦ region state, mailbox), and the log L.

Scheduling is a tick: tasks are ordered by id (6.6) and each runnable task takes exactly one communication step: it runs pure code until its next channel operation, spawn, select, emit or termination, and then performs that operation. All operations of a tick are staged and delivered after every task has moved (Form law 2: every update reads the pre-state). A tick is logged as Tick{n} plus one entry per communication action, with payloads (Form law 4).

  c has space                     ─→ v appended to c.buffer; task continues
  c full                          ─→ (c, v) held in c.held in arrival order;
                                     task blocked; Backpressure logged (no drop, law 3)
  <- c, buffer nonempty           ─→ first value; held send released in order
  <- c, empty and closed          ─→ none
  <- c, empty and open            ─→ task blocked
  spawn f(ā)                      ─→ new task id h(…); args moved in
  select: ready arms R ≠ ∅        ─→ execution k of this select statement in
                                     this task scans the arms cyclically from
                                     arm k mod n (n arms, source order) and
                                     takes the first ready one (draft 0.5)
  select: R = ∅, default present  ─→ default arm
  select: R = ∅, `after n`        ─→ blocked; after n ticks with R still ∅, after-arm

An actor is a region with a mailbox; a <- M(v) is an event M(v) admitted to a's region at the next tick; the actor runs its handlers by 6.4 with its own region as S. Each actor processes at most one message per tick, in mailbox order.

Fairness (draft 0.5). The counter k is per task and per select statement, starts at 0 and grows by one per execution. An arm that is ready at each of n consecutive executions of its select is taken by one of them (bounded wait). Draft 0.4 always took the minimal arm, so a busy first channel could starve the others, the problem Go solves with a random choice; the rotation gives the same guarantee without randomness. Lean: RCE/Select.lean (select_bounded_wait).

Because the order of every choice is a function of ids, payloads and per-select counters, and ids are content hashes, the entire run of a program is a function of its inputs: replaying the log reproduces it (T1, T3). The host may run tasks in parallel provided the observable result equals the tick semantics.

Deadlock: a tick in which no task can move and no input is pending ends the run with outcome Deadlock in λ (a defined outcome, not a hang).

sections.title: 6.9 Examples and checks
sections.html:
example ē -> o denotes the proposition: folding the events ē from s₀ gives a final step whose outcome is o. The fold is the one of rce run and of the host (HC-21): a step that keeps the state leaves it unchanged (T8) and the next event is applied to that state, so an earlier event of ē may be kept or applied and the proposition is about the last step and the state after it. For -> kept: X the last step is kept with the error X, for -> kept: trap("K") the last step is kept by the trap K, and for -> e the last step is applied and then

  • if the program has exactly one region with exactly one field f, the value of f equals ⟦e⟧;
  • otherwise e must be a bool expression over the final state, with fields in scope by name (or R.f when ambiguous), and must be true.

Example: the counter spec/examples/01_counter.rce states example Dec, Inc -> 1: Dec is kept with Underflow, the state stays s₀, and Inc applies to it. Until the change of 2026-10-31 (ledger), an example held only when every event before the last was applied, and rce run and rce trace ended at the first kept step; the examples that held then hold now, with the same traces, and an example whose earlier event is kept is now a statement about the fold that goes on past it. An author who wants an earlier step stated writes the prefix as an example of its own.

check e (in an intent or at comptime) is the proposition ⟦e⟧ = true, evaluated at comptime. A program is admitted only if every example and check holds (W-INT-1): the gate is part of the language, not of a test harness. Derivation of the trap form: a step ends in a value, a named error or a trap (T2), so a proposition about one final step needs all three outcomes, or a program whose specified behavior is a trap has no example that states it and no emitted program can be held to it.

The lookup-table control (W-INT-2). The examples of a module are finitely many event lists folded from s₀, so they say nothing about any other list. The lookup-table control of a module M is M with one more field per region, the region's position in the trie of the example event lists (each list restricted to the events the region has a step for and that M applies when it folds the list): a step that M keeps, the control keeps with the same error; each step that M applies, the control applies only at a position that has a child for its event and moves the position to that child (where M selects no step of the region, the control only moves the position), and an event that M applies at a position with no child for it is kept with an error of its own. The control equals M on every prefix of every example list, so it meets every example of M, and it keeps the state on every other list. A check is a proposition about comptime values and functions, and a contract (F.6.2) is a proposition about a function, and the control keeps both unchanged, so neither tells M from its control. Hence, when a module has a step and example lines, rce check admits it and reports the recommended change W-INT-2 (10.2): its obligations do not constrain behaviour beyond the listed examples. A module with a law (6.11) has an obligation beyond them, and W-INT-2 is not reported for it. W-INT-2 never makes a program require change; it says what the examples do not state.

sections.title: 6.10 Behaviour, equivalence and dimension
sections.html:
This section defines what "the same behaviour" means for two programs, and the dimension of a program: the number of behaviours it can be in. Example: a counter with a field that no step reads has the dimension of the counter without it.

In plain words: (1) the behaviour of a program is the answer it gives to every sequence of events; two programs are the same when their answers are the same, and that is the only sense of "same" the Form needs; (2) two different behaviours disagree at some first step, and a test that checks the first k steps shows the programs are within 2^-(k+1) of each other, not that they are equal; (3) the dimension of a program is the number of different behaviours it can be in, and state that cannot change any future answer is redundancy the checker can count.

Behaviour. Fix a program P with state space S, event alphabet E and δ : S × E → S × O* (6.1), δ₁ = π₁ ∘ δ, λ = π₂ ∘ δ. The behaviour of a state s is the function beh_P(s) : E* → (O*)* with beh_P(s)(ε) = ε and beh_P(s)(e · w) = λ(s, e) · beh_P(δ₁(s, e))(w): the sequence of per-step outputs along any event sequence. The behaviour of P is beh_P(s₀). Derivation: (S, ⟨λ, δ₁⟩) is a coalgebra of the functor F(X) = (O* × X)^E; F has a final coalgebra Beh whose carrier is the set of such functions, and beh_P is the unique coalgebra morphism S → Beh (Rutten 2000, Theorem 2.3). Every Form, in every fit language, maps into the same Beh by the same construction, so Beh is the one object every projection targets.

Equivalence. Two fits F and G are equivalent, F ≡ G, when beh_F(s₀^F) = beh_G(s₀^G). A relation R ⊆ S_F × S_G is a bisimulation when s R t implies, for every e ∈ E, λ_F(s, e) = λ_G(t, e) and δ₁^F(s, e) R δ₁^G(t, e). T58 says ≡ is bisimilarity, so a proof of ≡ exhibits a bisimulation, and a proof of ≢ exhibits a distinguishing event sequence.

Distance. For behaviours b₁, b₂ let n(b₁, b₂) be the length of the shortest event sequence on which they differ (∞ when equal) and d(b₁, b₂) = 2^-n. This is the prefix ultrametric (de Bakker and Zucker 1982): complete and totally disconnected. Trace agreement on every sequence of length ≤ k (the evidence of T9) certifies d ≤ 2^-(k+1), a ball around the behaviour and not the behaviour; trace evidence therefore never enters a hash or a key.

Dimension. reach(P) = {s : ∃ w ∈ E*, s = foldl(δ₁, s₀, w)} is finite (6.3 N9). dim(P) = |{beh_P(s) : s ∈ reach(P)}| is the number of distinct behaviours P can be in; log₂ dim(P) is the bits of state the behaviour needs, and log₂ |reach(P)| − log₂ dim(P) is the redundancy of the fit, the bits of state that change no future answer. dim(P) is the number of states of the minimal Mealy machine with behaviour beh_P(s₀) (the Nerode index; Nerode 1958, Moore 1956, Hopcroft 1971), unique up to isomorphism because δ is total and deterministic (T1, T2); an incompletely specified machine has no unique minimum (Pfleeger 1973).

Control dimension. Let S = Σc × Σd (6.1). The control projection P_c replaces every guard over Σd by its predicate symbol and every data update by a symbolic update, giving a symbolic finite automaton over the guard predicates of 6.4 (D'Antoni and Veanes 2014). dim_c(P) is the Nerode index of P_c modulo predicate equivalence; dim_c(P) ≤ dim(P). The symbolic quotient is not implemented; rce dim control (10.11) computes the control quotient of the explored concrete machine instead.

Canonical control form. Let M_c be the minimal machine of P_c, its states numbered by first visit in a breadth-first traversal from s₀ taking events in declaration order (the name-free key of 6.6) and payloads in the order of their columns in the explored alphabet of 10.11 (Reis, Moreira and Almeida 2005: the canonical string of an initially connected DFA is unique and name-free by construction). shape_ctl(P) is the SHA-256 over the canonical JSON (6.1.1) of that string. shape_ctl equal means the same control behaviour up to predicate equivalence; ≡ means the same behaviour, decidable for finite S by partition refinement on reach(P) and in practice bounded by the exploration fuel of rce dim (10.11). The proposal form-ir-2.md names two further keys, a name-free term hash and an e-class key, that this text does not define.

sections.title: 6.11 Laws
sections.html:
A law states a property of every state a program reaches, or of every step taken from such a state, and the checker decides it before the program is admitted. Example: the flag game of spec/proposals/laws.md states law you_cant_win with the claim always not won; with walls on the far edges of its board the checker explores its 72 reachable states and the law holds; without them it fails, and the report prints the 9 events that reach the flag as an example line.

In plain words: (1) an example states one sequence of events, and a law states something about every sequence, of every length; (2) the checker decides a law by visiting every state the program can reach, which is exact when it finishes and when it finds a violation; (3) a law it cannot decide within a fixed bound requires change, unless a named person attests it.

Meaning. Let s₀, δ, δ₁ and E be as in 6.1 and 6.10, and reach(P) the states that some sequence of events leads to from s₀. A law has one claim (3.2):

  • always p holds when ⟦p⟧ = true at every s ∈ reach(P). p is a bool expression over the state, with fields in scope by name, as in the -> e of an example (6.9).
  • every step [on PAT] [if g] -> o holds when, for every s ∈ reach(P) and every event instance e that matches PAT (every event, without on) and for which g is true at s, the step δ(s, e) has the outcome o. PAT is a step pattern (3.5) and binds its names for g and o; g is a bool over s. The outcome kept says the event is kept, kept: X that it is kept with the error X, and applied that it applies. An expression o is a bool over δ₁(s, e), the state after the step (s itself when the event is kept, T8), in which old(f) names the field f of s.

p, g and o may call the module's functions; they are checked as comptime expressions (5.4), so they call no foreign function. A trap while evaluating one of them is a violation at that state or step. By T3 every state a fold of events reaches is in reach(P), so a law over reach(P) is a law over every event sequence.

The complete alphabet. A payload field type is listable when the checker can list its values in full: bool, (), u8, i8, T? of a listable T, a kind without type parameters whose variants carry only listable fields, and a type declared type N = T or type N = T where p (5.1) of a listable T (a value outside p traps at construction and is no event). The alphabet of a program is every instance of every event whose fields are all listable, events in declaration order (the name-free key of 6.6) and the values of each field in their order: false before true, integers ascending, none before some, variants in declaration order, the fields of a payload varying last field fastest. An event with more than 4,096 instances, or with a field that is not listable, is left out, and the alphabet is then incomplete.

Method D1, exhaustive exploration. The checker explores reach(P) breadth first from s₀, applying every instance of the alphabet in its order to each state, and keys a state by its canonical JSON (6.1.1). It evaluates every always law at each new state, s₀ first, and every every step law at each step. It stops when every law has a violation, when no new state appears (the exploration is closed), or when a new state would be the (LAW_FUEL + 1)th. LAW_FUEL is a constant of the language, 1,000,000 states, so admission depends only on the program text (10.1, item 1), as with LOOP_LIMIT (6.7).

Verdicts. Each law gets one verdict:

  • holds: the exploration closed with no violation and the alphabet is complete. By T63 the law then holds after every event sequence of every length.
  • fails: a violation was found. The sequence that reaches it exists, so the verdict is exact whether or not the bound was reached and whether or not the alphabet is complete.
  • undecided: no violation, and the alphabet is incomplete or the bound was reached. The report names each event left out (Deposit.amount (u64)) and the bound.
  • attested: undecided, and attested (below).

A program is admitted only when every law holds or is attested (W-INT-1 for examples and checks, W-LAW-1 for laws). An attestation never changes a fails.

The counterexample. The sequence a failing law reports is the shortest one after which the law fails, and among the shortest the first in the order of the alphabet, compared event by event from the start: a breadth-first exploration that takes events in a fixed order meets the states in that order. It is printed as an example line (3.2) that states what the program does now, so it holds and can be pasted into an intent as it is: for always p, the outcome is not p (q when p is not q; the field's value when the state has one field of type bool); for an every step law, kept: X when the last step is kept with X, else the fields of the state after the last step with their values (x == 1 and won == true). Changing the outcome to the law's turns the line into the example that the corrected program must meet. For the flag game without walls:

requires change flag_wrap.rce: line 4: W-LAW-1 law you_cant_win fails after 9 events (exhaustive, alphabet 4 complete, 86 states explored): the claim is false [requires change]
    example Up, Up, Up, Up, Right, Right, Right, Right, Right -> won

Attestation. A line attest "WHO;YYYY-MM-DD;COVER" in a law says that the person WHO decided on that date that the law holds; it is the form of ui.rules (attest-ID) with the cover added. The cover of a law is a SHA-256 over the law's claim, with every named definition replaced by its definition hash (F.4.3), and over the sorted definition hashes of every state, event and error, of every step (by its text, with the definitions it names replaced by their hashes) and of every definition the claim names. An attestation applies only while its COVER equals the current cover: when a definition it covers changes, the attestation lapses and the law is undecided again. A definition that no step, no state, no event and no claim reaches can change without lapsing it. The report of an undecided law prints the current cover. An attest line that is not of this form requires change (W-LAW-1).

Reports. rce check reports each law that fails or is undecided and not attested under W-LAW-1, with the counterexample line. rce law FILE (10.11) prints one line per law with its verdict, the method and the counts, for example law you_cant_win holds exhaustive 72 states, 288 steps, alphabet 4 (complete), closed; its status is 0 when every law holds or is attested, 3 when the only obstacle is the bound, and 1 otherwise. rce change OLD NEW decides every law of OLD on NEW (10.11).

Laws are part of the canonical text, so they are in the program hash (10.8). The other methods of the proposal (an inductive invariant, a Lean proof) are not part of the language; a law that states liveness ("eventually") or a property of fn main and its tasks is not expressible.

chapters.title: 7. Well-formedness: what requires change at entry
chapters.question: Under which rule does a region with two unguarded steps whose patterns overlap require change?

sections.html:
This section is the checklist of rules a program must pass to be accepted (well-formedness). Each rule has a name such as W-TY-1, and a program that requires change is reported with the rule it broke. Example: a function declared -> i64 whose body returns text requires change: W-TY-1.

A program requires change if any rule fails. Every diagnostic names its rule.

Lexical and syntax

  • W-LEX-1 Not UTF-8, BOM, bare CR, or a tab character.
  • W-LEX-2 Inconsistent dedent (2.6).
  • W-LEX-3 A literal outside every possible type range, or an invalid \u{}.
  • W-SYN-1 Not in the language of section 3.
  • W-RES-1 A construct that a rule of this document specifies and this implementation does not implement (a reserved word used as its construct, F.12): requires change, with the words reserved, not implemented.

Names and modules

  • W-NAME-1 Unresolved name, or a name resolved in the wrong namespace.
  • W-NAME-2 Duplicate declaration in one scope; shadowing a parameter, field or module-level name inside the same item.
  • W-MOD-1 use of a private item; W-MOD-2 import cycle. The reference checker reports a private name reached through use as W-VIS-1, which is the same rule.
  • W-MOD-3 An import's name (q of use p.q, r of use p.q as r) that clashes with a declaration of the importing module or names two different modules. The items of an imported module are reached only through that name (4.1), so an item never clashes with the importer's items or with another module's, pub or not; use p.q as r resolves a clash.
  • W-SAFE-1 The identifiers unsafe, Rc, Arc, RefCell, transmute, static: requires change, with "memory safety is by construction" (there are no escape hatches in RCE other than the extern boundary of 5.11).
  • W-FFI-1 An extern declaration whose ABI is not "C", that is comptime or generic, or whose parameter or result types break 5.11; or a foreign function's name used other than as the callee of a direct call.

Types

  • W-TY-1 Any typing rule of section 5 fails.
  • W-TY-2 Nested option τ??; borrow of a borrow &&τ; [τ] not behind a borrow; a borrow, region type or fn type inside a data type.
  • W-TY-3 Integer/float mixing without as; implicit narrowing.
  • W-PAT-1 A binding pattern whose name equals a variant in scope.
  • W-MATCH-1 A non-exhaustive match (5.3 [Match]); W-MATCH-2 an unreachable arm (subsumed by earlier unguarded arms).
  • W-PLACE Left side of an assignment or op= is not a mutable place.

Ownership and borrowing

  • W-OWN-1 Use after move (O1). W-OWN-2 Violating [No-Alias-Write] or [No-Mut-Read]. W-OWN-3 Storing, returning (except R-RET) or capturing a borrow. W-REG-1 A region-typed value escaping its with arena block.
  • W-SPAWN-1 Spawning with a borrow or region-typed argument.

The Form

  • W-STATE-1 A state with no fields; W-STATE-2 a field initializer that is not a comptime constant; W-STATE-3 a field type that is not an owned data type.
  • W-STEP-1 A step naming an undeclared region or matching an undeclared event. W-STEP-2 Totality: an event that no step and no actor handler can ever match. W-STEP-3 The arrow form on a region with more than one field. W-STEP-4 Within one region, two unguarded steps whose patterns overlap (the second is unreachable).
  • W-EFF-1 emit, spawn, channel operations or select in a pure fn; reading another region's fields in a step; calling a foreign function anywhere but fn main or a task function.
  • W-REC-1 A cycle in the call graph, including through trait methods after monomorphization, other than a cycle of plain functions (one function calling itself included) whose calls are done by layered summed measures, or each of whose cycles of calls passes through a function declared with bound (6.7); par or for … par in a function of a cycle with a bounded function; bound on an iterator, a foreign function or a trait signature.
  • W-CT-1 Comptime code that calls a non-comptime-safe function or traps or exceeds fuel.
  • W-INT-1 An example or check that does not hold.
  • W-INT-2 (recommended; never requires change) A module with a step and example lines, whose obligations its lookup-table control meets (6.9): rce check admits it and prints the recommendation (10.2).
  • W-LAW-1 A law (6.11) that fails, or that is undecided and not attested (its alphabet is incomplete or the bound LAW_FUEL is reached), or an attest line that is not WHO;YYYY-MM-DD;COVER. The report of a failing law ends with its counterexample as an example line. The trait laws of F.6.6 fall under the same rule once they are implemented.
  • W-SIMD-1 A lane-wise operator on arrays of different lengths, of an unfixed length, or with non-numeric lanes (5.1).
  • W-LIN-1 A linear value not consumed exactly once on every path, copied, moved inside a loop, or placed in a collection, field, payload, channel or iterator (5.12).
  • W-DEV-1 A growable value (List, Map, Set, text, slice, channel, iterator) bound in a device region, or emit, spawn, send, select, yield or a foreign call inside one (5.13).
  • W-ITER-1 An iterator function that is not pure or has an arrow body; yield outside an iterator function; an iter τ value used other than as a for operand or .collect() receiver (5.14).
  • W-REF-1 A refined type (5.1) that is generic, refines a type other than an integer type, text or a collection, or whose predicate is outside the decidable fragment (a term other than self, self.len() or an integer literal, an operator other than a comparison, and, or, not, or a call other than a text character class).
  • W-LOOP-1 A LOOP_LIMIT declaration that is not const LOOP_LIMIT: u64 = n with a positive literal n (6.7).
  • W-TRAIT-1 An impl not matching its trait; W-TRAIT-2 incoherent or orphan impls; W-TRAIT-3 a type used with ==, !=, an ordering operator or a generic bound without implementing the trait it needs.

Indexed values (5.16)

  • W-CTX-1 Context text made other than by C.lit of a string literal or C.encode; joined with another context or plain text; carried by an event payload; an unknown context.
  • W-SEC-1 An operator or method on a secret other than ==/!=; a secret in an emitted value, a channel, an error payload or a foreign call.
  • W-CAP-1 A capability outside an event payload field or a parameter; Guarded outside a state field; an authority that is not a declared struct.
  • W-CAP-2 A step that writes a Guarded[τ, A] field on an event without a Cap[A] field. (A declaration named after a 5.16 type or context requires change: W-NAME-2.)

Appendix F (specified and implemented in part, F.12): the rules of F.3 to F.8 under which a text requires change, among them unused values, dropped results and shadowing (F.3), World and information-flow labels (F.4), transactional calls (F.4), capabilities, typed output, pinned builds, constant-time functions and budgets (F.5), and templates, contracts, ghost code, written measures, if let and trait laws (F.6). Their names and rules are listed where each is defined and are not repeated here, so that this list names only rules the reference checker implements.

Concurrency (Appendix C): W-PAR-1 to W-PAR-4, W-DL-1, W-ND-1, W-GRP-1 to W-GRP-3, W-SES-1 to W-SES-5, W-SCOPE-1, W-ATOM-1, W-ATOM-2, W-CRDT-1, W-LVAR-1, W-LVAR-2, W-NODE-1, W-SUP-1, W-SUP-2, W-INTR-1 and W-RT-1.

sections.title: 7.1 How a rule guides a program into Form
sections.html:
Each rule of this section, of Appendix C and of Appendix F guides a program that does not meet it into Form by exactly one of three methods:

  • Altered. The rule has one rewrite, determined by the text, that keeps the program's meaning. rce fmt FILE writes it and rce fmt check FILE lists it (10.6). Until it is written the text requires change, and rce check ends the report with [altered by rce fmt] (10.2). A rewrite that would add or change another report is not written; rce fmt then prints the report as requiring change.
  • Recommended. The program is admitted, and rce check prints a recommended line that names the rule and the change (10.2).
  • Requires change. The program is not admitted until its author changes it, because the change has more than one reading or states something only the author can state (a type, a declaration, a bound, an authority). rce check ends the report with [requires change].

A rule is altered only when the reference rce fmt writes its rewrite. The table gives every rule its method; the checker reads it from spec/data/spec-data.json (w_methods), and tests/three_methods.rs checks that every rule of the three lists has exactly one row and that the altered rows are the rules rce fmt rewrites. Name independence (T7, section 8) is the ground of a rewrite that renames.

sections.html:
This section states the properties the language guarantees, such as determinism and termination, and records which are proved in Lean 4 (a proof assistant that checks proofs by machine). A theorem here is a statement about every well-formed program. Example: T8 (atomicity) says an event that does not apply leaves the state exactly as it was.

Stated for well-formed programs (section 7). Proofs are mechanized in Lean 4 (v4.12.0, no Mathlib) in spec/lean/, over a core calculus: expressions (RCE/Expr.lean), statements, steps, regions, δ and the runtime fold (RCE/Form.lean), typing of steps and states (RCE/Typing.lean), an ownership core (RCE/Ownership.lean), the concurrency rules of 6.8 (RCE/Conc.lean), full borrow paths (RCE/Borrow.lean), the step bound (RCE/Bound.lean), name-free hashing and ids (RCE/NameFree.lean) and the Rust emitter (RCE/Emit.lean, printer RCE/EmitPrint.lean, differential harness emit-test/), structural recursion (RCE/Struct.lean, draft 0.4), mutual recursion (RCE/Mutual.lean), and the draft 0.5 additions: select fairness (RCE/Select.lean), linear handles (RCE/Linear.lean), f32 (RCE/F32.lean), u64 arithmetic (RCE/U64.lean) and iterators (RCE/Iter.lean), and foreign replay (RCE/Replay.lean), &mut write-back (RCE/WriteBack.lean), bound composition (RCE/Compose.lean) and the host contract of Appendix E (RCE/Host.lean). Build with lake build; no sorry, no added axioms (#print axioms lists only propext, Quot.sound, Classical.choice). Status per theorem:

T16 to T31 belong to the concurrency part (Appendix C) and are listed with their exact status in Appendix C.13. Most are proofs about abstract models (T18, T19b, T21, T22, T25 to T27, T29 to T31); T16, T17, T19a, T20 and T23 are proved on a small-step semantics of a core with par; none is a proof about the Rust reference evaluator.

T1 Determinism. For every program P, state s and event e there is exactly one (s′, o) with δ_P(s, e) = (s′, o). For a command, the full configuration sequence of 6.8 is a function of the input events. ∀ s e r₁ r₂. ⟨step P, s, e⟩ ⇓ r₁ ∧ ⟨step P, s, e⟩ ⇓ r₂ ⇒ r₁ = r₂.

T2 Totality of δ. For every s ∈ S and e ∈ E, evaluation of δ(s, e) terminates, and the number of evaluation steps is at most B_P(size(s) + size(e)) for a function B_P computable from P (from loop bounds, SIZE_LIMIT and the call graph, which is acyclic except for recursive cycles admitted by layered measures or declared bounds, 6.7). When the call graph has no cycle, B_P(n) = B(P) · (1 + n). A recursive cycle contributes the number of calls of a chain of calls, which is finite because its tuple of measures falls in a well-founded order, and bounded by a function of the sizes of the values it recurses on, themselves bounded by N9; that function need not be linear (a function that calls itself twice on the same component makes a number of calls exponential in the size).

T3 Fold law. For every log D = e₁…eₙ, the state the runtime reaches is foldl(δ₁, s₀, D), and replaying D from s₀ reproduces every state hash and every output: ∀ D. run(P, D) = foldl(δ, s₀, D) componentwise.

T4 Progress. If ∅; Γ ⊢ e : τ and the store σ agrees with Γ, then ⟨e, ρ, σ⟩ steps, or e is a value, or e is a trap, fail, ret, brk or cont signal. (No stuck states other than defined outcomes.) For configurations of 6.8: either some task can move, or the run ends with a defined outcome (all tasks done, or Deadlock).

T5 Preservation. If Σ; Γ; Δ ⊢ e : τ ⊣ Γ′ and e → e′ (small-step presentation of 6.2), then there is Δ′ with Σ; Γ; Δ′ ⊢ e′ : τ ⊣ Γ′; and every value written to a state field of type τ is in ⟦τ⟧ (including its integer range).

T6 Memory safety. A well-typed program never reads a value after it has been dropped or moved, never observes a write through one path while another path to the same location is live (shared XOR mutable, 5.6), never reads a region after it is freed (5.7), and never shares mutable data between tasks (5.8). Formally: in the instrumented semantics that tags each location with an owner and a validity bit, no well-typed program reaches a configuration where an access touches an invalid location or two tasks hold a mutable path to one location. Foreign functions (5.11) are outside this statement: T6 holds for the RCE side under the 5.11 contract on the callee. (Approach: RustBelt-style semantic typing is not needed because borrows are second class; a syntactic progress/preservation proof over the instrumented semantics suffices.)

T7 Name independence. If P′ is P with identifiers consistently renamed, then every log hash, every id and every select choice of P′ equals that of P.

T8 Atomicity. If e does not apply in s (δ(s, e) keeps the state), then δ₁(s, e) = s.

T9 Implementation agreement (per target). For every target t, ⟦compile_t(P)⟧ = δ_P on every s, e, including every edge of 6.3. There are two target sets, and a claim names its set. T9-F: the Form IR targets of the compiler (rce form --emit): Rust (native), WASM (the Rust crate on wasm32-wasip1), Python, XState and SCXML. T9-L: the program emitters of 10.5 (rce emit rust | python | js), which translate the checked module. A target outside these sets has no T9 claim. This is the theorem the differential tests sample; it is stated here so it is clear those tests check a property of implementations, not of the language. A differential test compares against the reference evaluator's trace, which the target under test does not produce.

T10 Grammar unambiguity. The grammar of section 3 is LALR(1) (checked mechanically, 3.12), hence unambiguous: every accepted text has exactly one parse tree. The same holds for the grammar with the concurrency productions (section 3 with Appendix C.2 applied), checked by the same machine.

T11 Select fairness (bounded wait). An arm of a select that is ready at each of n consecutive executions of that select (n arms) is taken by one of them.

T12 Linear use. In a well-formed program every value of a linear type is consumed exactly once on every execution path.

T13 f32 determinism. Every f32 operation gives the same binary32 result on every conforming target.

T14 u64 arithmetic. A u64 operation returns the exact mathematical result when it lies in [0, 2^64) and traps otherwise.

T15 Iterator termination. A for loop over an iterator, and .collect(), terminate after at most LOOP_LIMIT yields, and break observes a prefix of the values the iterator would produce.

T57 Finality. beh_P of 6.10 is a coalgebra morphism: beh_P(s)(e · w) = λ(s, e) · beh_P(δ₁(s, e))(w), and it is the unique such map S → Beh.

T58 Equivalence is bisimilarity. beh_P(s) = beh_P(t) if and only if there is a bisimulation R with s R t; likewise for two programs on S_F × S_G.

T59 Trace evidence is a ball. If beh_F(s₀)(w) = beh_G(s₀)(w) for every w with |w| ≤ k, then d(beh_F, beh_G) ≤ 2^-(k+1), and conversely.

T60 Minimal machine. For finite S, the quotient of reach(P) by the largest bisimulation is a Mealy machine with the behaviour beh_P(s₀) and dim(P) states; every Mealy machine with that behaviour has at least dim(P) states, with equality only up to isomorphism; the canonical numbering of 6.10 makes the isomorphism class one string.

T61 Control canonicity. shape_ctl (6.10) is invariant under renaming (T7) and under any rewrite of a guard to a predicate-equivalent guard; it is not invariant under a change of a data update that changes a later guard outcome.

T62 Linearization invariance (proposal). For a layer of D between two cuts, any two orders that agree with every chain's seq order and every deps edge fold δ₁ to the same state at the upper cut (spec/proposals/partial-order-log.md).

T63 Exploration decides a law. Let the alphabet of 6.11 be complete and let C be a finite set of states with s₀ ∈ C that every instance of the alphabet takes into C. If a property holds at every state of C, it holds at foldl(δ₁, s₀, w) for every event sequence w, and an every step property that holds at every step from a state of C holds at every step from every reached state. A sequence w after which the property is false refutes the law. When every state of C is reached from s₀, the law holds for every sequence exactly when it holds on C (6.11, method D1).

T32 Foreign replay. For every oracle o answering foreign calls and select nondet choices (5.11, C.5), replaying the log of a live run reproduces its state, whatever o is; no property of the foreign code is assumed, and a contract every answer satisfies holds of every logged answer.

T33 &mut restore on failure (F.4.4). A call that ends by fail leaves the caller's &mut state as it was at the call, and a call that returns writes the callee's final value back. This is proved of a model that copies in, runs on the copy and copies out only when the outcome is a value. The rule that wrote back on every outcome, which this number used to state, is retired and is no longer in the proved tree. That every effect since entry is undoable is W-TX-1, a check of the checker; T42 to T56 state the remaining properties; T48, T51 and T53 are proved of models (RCE/Discharged.lean) and the other twelve are unproved.

T36 Indexed values. (5.16): untrusted text forms no structure of a Text[C] value; outputs do not depend on secrets beyond the equality bits; a guarded field changes only on events that carry its capability.

T35 Refinement invariance. If the initial state satisfies the predicates of its refined fields, every state in the fold of the log (6.1) satisfies them, and an event whose payload or resulting state breaks a predicate does not apply, with the state unchanged (5.1).

T37 Host replay. For every adapter oracle, replaying the log D with every adapter disconnected gives the live run's state after every entry; host entries leave the state unchanged; placement, a function of the logged host entries, is the same on replay (Appendix E).

T38 Verify on open. The verified prefix of a hash-chained log is a prefix of it and a valid chain, equals the log when the log is valid, and cuts a valid log followed by an entry that does not link back to the valid log (Appendix E, HS-4).

T39 Fatal barrier. After a failed storage barrier the admitter appends nothing more, and a running admitter's log holds exactly the entries it was given (Appendix E, HS-3).

T34 Order-preserving A-normal form. Flattening an expression into let-bound steps in left-to-right order, with each temporary fresh, gives the same value, final store, and ordered trace of budget charges and emits as evaluating the expression.

T42 to T56 are stated in Appendix F.9 and are obligations of Appendix F. T48, T51 and T53 are proved, each of a small model of its rule (spec/lean/RCE/Discharged.lean, in lake build and the audit); a model proof says the rule is coherent, not that the checker or an emitter implements it. The other twelve are not proved: their statements as Lean Props over abstract model records are in spec/lean/obligations/Obligations.lean; that file has no theorem, is not part of lake build and is not read by scripts/lean-audit.sh, so the audit counts do not include it.

Numbering and assurance. Theorem numbers are stable identifiers, not positions: a number is never reused or changed, new theorems take the next number (T32 on), and a split keeps its number with a letter (T19a, T19b). Code, tests, Lean doc comments and papers cite these numbers, so renumbering would break every citation for no gain in meaning. Each row's status uses one of the levels proved (Lean, on the RCE semantics or the named core), model (Lean, on an abstract model), checked (a machine check that is exhaustive for its input, such as LALR(1)), tested (sampled differential or property tests), in that order, with stated, unproved below them for a theorem whose statement is written but which has no Lean statement, no test and no checker rule yet (T42 to T56, Appendix F.9; T59 over all of E, T60 and T61, 6.10); such a row is an obligation and never a claim. A counterexample is a failure, never a lower level, and a claim about several parts has the lowest level among them. Every Lean name in the tables is checked to exist (spec/checker/tests/theorem_index.rs).

chapters.title: 9. Design decisions for review
chapters.question: The decisions list says it decides gaps in which file?

sections.html:
This section lists the design choices the spec makes, each with a one-line reason, and the changes made in each draft. Each decision can be reviewed and reversed on its own. Example: decision 45 makes text indexed by UTF-8 byte, as in Go, Rust and Zig.

Gaps in SURFACE.md that this spec decides. Each is one line of rationale; each can be reversed independently.

  1. Layout by indentation, spaces only, tabs require change (Python), with brackets suspending layout. Keeps SURFACE.md's look; tabs removed to make layout unambiguous.

  2. # comments only, matching the prototype; no block comments.

  3. Case-sensitive event names in examples. The prototype wrote example inc for event Inc; the spec requires Inc (no hidden case mapping).

  4. Several state regions per program, each step reading only its own region (pre-state, ASM), events atomic across regions. Matches Form law 2 and the "rules read their own sink" limit.

  5. Totality = every event is handled somewhere; unmatched regions are unchanged. Stricter than "every (region, event) pair", looser than "every event in every region"; catches typos without boilerplate.

  6. Errors keep the state: the event does not apply (example … -> kept: X), and are logged and output, never thrown.

  7. Traps (overflow, division by zero, non-finite, index, size, loop bound) are Form errors, not part of declared error sets; catch cannot hide them.

  8. Recursion only where it provably ends (revised in 0.4 and later: a self-call passes a constructor field of a matched parameter, or a measure falls in layers, including mutual recursion, or the cycle carries a declared bound; 6.7 says exactly which) and every loop bounded (default 1,000,000, bound n to change), so δ is total by construction. (Originally structural recursion only, with mutual recursion requiring change.)

  9. Second-class borrows, no lifetime syntax. Borrows only in parameters, receivers, loop/match operands and short lets, plus borrow returns tied to a parameter. Simpler than Rust, still no GC and no aliasing of mutable state.

  10. struct only, no class; value semantics, explicit copy() for deep duplication of non-Copy values.

  11. Integer types checked against their own range, lowered to the Form's i64, except u64, which uses the Form's unsigned operations and is exact over [0, 2^64) (6.3 N2, T14; draft 0.5). No implicit widening; no literal suffixes. (Originally u64 results at or above 2^63 trapped.)

  12. f64 is the Form's float. f32 was added in draft 0.5 (decision 42): it is computed in f64 and rounded once. (Originally f64 only.)

  13. Bitwise operators bind tighter than comparisons (unlike C/Python's & vs == in C), so x & 1 == 1 means what it reads as.

  14. if … then … else … as the expression conditional; no Python a if c else b (it collides with try … else).

  15. try e, try e else E, e catch d, e catch |x| h as the error vocabulary (Zig plus the prototype's else).

  16. Option is T? with some(x) / none.

  17. Generic arguments in square brackets (List[T], f[T](x)), Go-style, resolved by name resolution; impl parameters need forall.

  18. Argument labels Swift-style (fn move(from src: u8)), optional when the label equals the parameter name.

  19. comptime for consts, array lengths, state initializers, comptime parameters, and comptime blocks/expressions; comptime is pure and deterministic.

  20. Arenas are lexical (with arena r), region-typed values cannot escape; each step has an implicit per-step arena.

  21. Concurrency is deterministic by construction: ticks, staged delivery, content-hash ids, select takes the first ready arm from a rotating start (decision 48), bounded channels with held sends and Backpressure logs (no silent drop), after n in logical ticks, Deadlock is a defined outcome. (Originally select chose the least ready arm; it rotates its starting arm since draft 0.5, decision 48 and T11. par and the rest of C.4 are in version 0.6.)

  22. Pure functions cannot emit, spawn or use channels; only steps, handlers, main and task functions (those with a chan parameter) have effects (revised by S2).

  23. Actors are regions with mailboxes and handlers (on M(…)), one message per tick.

  24. A program with fn main and no state is a command: one event Start(args), outputs are its emits.

  25. Examples and checks are part of admission (the gate), and the outcome of a multi-field example is a boolean over the final state.

  26. Kind variants encode as {"$v": name, …} records in Form values; maps/sets as sorted lists, so canonical JSON hashing stays well-defined.

  27. Identifiers are ASCII; text values are full Unicode, case operations ASCII-only (as num.rs).

  28. No macros, no exceptions, no null, no inheritance, no operator overloading beyond traits Eq/Ord/Show: kept out to keep one meaning per text.

  29. The grammar artifact is the EBNF of section 3, checked LALR(1) by rce-spec-check: a deterministic LR table with mechanical conflict detection, with a tree-sitter port checked against it. (Originally a Lark file, rce.lark, now retired.)

  30. Tail values in block-bodied functions (S5).

  31. A trapping guard keeps the state (S1).

  32. Keywords reserved everywhere except after . (S3).

  33. std.text, std.collections, std.math are built-in modules (S4).

  34. Loop elements of non-Copy type are borrows; storing one needs copy(x); lists, constructors, channels and vars cannot hold borrows (W-OWN-3, made explicit by the checker). Map get returns V ! Missing.

  35. Structural recursion admitted (R1). Bound: calls ≤ nodes of the value recursed on.

  36. C-ABI extern functions (R2): scalars and borrowed buffers in, scalars out, no allocator crosses the boundary, callable only from main and task functions, results logged for replay. Unwinding across the boundary does not exist because RCE has no unwinding.

  37. Arena capacity with arena r bound n in canonical bytes (R3).

  38. Explicit wrapping_* and saturating_* methods (R4); + - * stay checked in every build (there is no build profile that changes meaning).

  39. &Box[τ] coerces to &τ (R5).

  40. Effects stay inferred from context (5.2), with no effect annotations and no async/await; a task function is an ordinary function that has a channel parameter.

  41. Ownership stays affine, not linear, except for types declared linear (decision 46): ordinary values drop with no observable effect (O4).

  42. f32 computed in f64, rounded once (N3). Bit-identical on every target; the cost is one extra rounding instruction per operation.

  43. Lane-wise arithmetic on fixed arrays instead of a separate vector type; the array length is the lane count.

  44. Device regions are placement hints with CPU meaning; only fixed-size, effect-free code may run in them.

  45. Text indexed by UTF-8 byte, with character-boundary checks on slices.

  46. Linear structs for outside resources, consumed exactly once.

  47. Full-range u64 through dedicated unsigned Form ops.

  48. select rotates its starting arm per execution instead of choosing at random (Go) or always the least (draft 0.4).

  49. LOOP_LIMIT is a per-program constant with default 1,000,000.

  50. Push iterators (Go 1.23) rather than pull generators (Python, Rust): no suspended state, so δ stays total and replay needs nothing new.

  51. Floats derived from IEEE 754-2019 and totality (6.3 N3, F1 to F9): correctly rounded basic operations only, one rounding per operator, subnormals kept, non-finite results trap because NaN and infinities break equality, order and JSON encoding, and transcendentals only as correctly rounded RCE code in the math module (F9), so every target runs the same algorithm instead of its platform library.

  52. Unicode 18.0.0 pinned, no tables read at run time (6.3 N7): the whitespace set and the display escape set are enumerated, so a toolchain upgrade cannot change a result.

  53. Draft 0.9 is a new release (label 0.9, never reuse 0.6), because it requires change in programs 0.8 accepted and changes &mut after a failed call (C.15 rule). Superseded in form by decision 64: the label gates nothing.

  54. A failed call restores its &mut arguments when every effect since entry is undoable; a function that could fail after a non-undoable effect requires change (F.4.4).

  55. Contracts are always enforced and a violation is one defined kept outcome with fixed fields; no switchable contracts (F.2, F.6.2).

  56. Information flow is checked by labels with a kept-outcome channel and robust declassification; labels are erased at run time (F.4.2).

  57. World is a borrowed capability, not a threaded value (F.4.1).

  58. The definition hash covers everything that affects meaning and nothing else (F.4.3).

  59. decreases is required only where 6.7 does not already admit the recursion, and never replaces the loop bound (F.6.4).

  60. Unused values, dropped results and shadowing require change in 0.9 (F.3).

  61. The four constructs that would break a theorem are written as non-goals: effect handlers, switchable contracts, mutable aliasing across par, runtime reflection (F.2).

  62. The relaxed sequential borrow rule is not adopted until its T6 lemma (T56) is proved (5.6).

  63. New theorems T42 to T56 are numbered after T41 and are stated, unproved; the survey's "T17" for noninterference became T42 because T17 is the par diamond lemma (F.9).

  64. One language, one text. The language is the text of one spec commit; # rce-version: is a release label, tolerated, ignored and not hashed (2.7), and a label names exactly one spec commit (C.15). No module selects older rules; one global reserved list (2.4); a construct that is specified and not implemented requires change as reserved, not implemented (W-RES-1). Derivation: one meaning per construct (F, principle e) forbids a program meaning two things depending on a comment, and the cost of a version-mixed program (C.15 of the earlier text) was exactly such a dependence. The standard library was migrated once (label to lbl, Json to JsonDoc, Url to UrlParts and the other renamed names); the mapping is in the stdlib README.

sections.title: 9.1 Changes made while mechanizing (draft 0.1 → 0.2)
sections.html:
• S1 (6.4) A guard that traps keeps the state. Draft 0.1 did not say; δ was not total on that case.
  • S2 (5.2) Task functions. Draft 0.1 decision 22 made every function except main pure, so spawn f(…) could never be well-typed; a function with a chan parameter may now use effects and be spawned.
  • S3 (2.4) Keywords are reserved (the Lark grammar now uses a basic lexer, so the machine grammar agrees with the text), except as member names after .. Example 25 now uses labels source/target since from is a keyword.
  • S4 (4.1) Built-in standard modules, so use std.text resolves.
  • S5 (5.3) Tail values in block-bodied functions; examples 05, 06, 23 and 29 relied on this reading.
  • Examples were made whole programs: declared errors (18, 19, 22) and the emitted records (04, 31), defined report (07) and depth_shallow (29), added shop_pricing.rce for 26, parenthesized (try …) as u32 (07) and (m.get(w) catch 0) + 1 (21, which previously meant catch (0 + 1)), copy(i) in 16, and 08/09 declare their own trait Describe (the built-in Show cannot be re-declared or given an orphan impl).

sections.title: 9.2 Changes in draft 0.3
sections.html:
• The admission gate of 6.9 is implemented: rce-check evaluates every example and check, every comptime block and every constant and state initializer, and reports that a program requires change on W-INT-1 or W-CT-1. W-LEX-3 (an integer literal outside its type's range) is checked.
  • rce.lark tree shapes (the language is unchanged): T? now yields an opt_type node, negative and true/false/none literal patterns, the three receiver forms (self, &self, &mut self), the two ends of a slice and e() versus e in example event lists are distinguishable in the tree. Draft 0.2 trees dropped these; found while porting to tree-sitter.

What the mechanized models simplify (stated so the coverage is clear): within a tick, sends are staged but receives consume in task-id order; select is modelled over channel ids only; actor state is a number; the borrow model's static context has the shape of the run-time state; H is an arbitrary function (no collision or SHA-256 model); concurrency is not evaluable at comptime.

sections.title: 9.3 Changes in draft 0.4 (from `spec/LANGUAGE-REVIEW.md`)
sections.html:
• R1 (6.7, W-REC-1) Structural self-recursion is admitted; mutual recursion and every other cycle still require change. Checker: structural_violation, since replaced by lex_measure (6.7: one fixed position, or layers). Lean: RCE/Struct.lean.
  • R2 (5.11, W-FFI-1, extern) A C-ABI foreign function interface: scalar and borrowed-buffer parameters, scalar results, callable only from main and task functions, results logged and replayed. extern is a new keyword.
  • R3 (5.7) with arena r bound n: an arena capacity in canonical bytes, exceeded by trap("size limit"). The checker types n as u64; the reference evaluator does not yet count arena bytes.
  • R4 (6.3 N2) wrapping_* and saturating_* integer methods; the default stays checked.
  • R5 (5.1) &Box[τ] coerces to &τ, which structural recursion over Box fields needs.

Draft 0.4 deferred the changes in 9.4 because each changes the Form or the emitters.

sections.title: 9.4 Changes in draft 0.5
sections.html:
• f32 (5.1, 6.3 N3): new type, Form ops f32add f32sub f32mul f32div and prim tof32 in form/num.rs, form_core.py and form_core.js. Lean: RCE/F32.lean.
  • Lane-wise array arithmetic (5.1, W-SIMD-1). It lowers to Form Map over the zipped lanes, so the Form needed no change.
  • Device regions (5.13, W-DEV-1, keyword device).
  • Byte-indexed text (5.1, 6.3 N7): Form prims blen, bget, bslice.
  • Full-range u64 (6.3 N2): Form ops uadd usub umul udiv urem. Lean: RCE/U64.lean.
  • select rotation and bounded wait (6.8). Lean: RCE/Select.lean.
  • Linear structs (5.12, W-LIN-1, keyword linear); extern may take and return linear structs with one scalar field. Lean: RCE/Linear.lean.
  • const LOOP_LIMIT: u64 = n (6.7, W-LOOP-1).
  • Iterators (5.14, W-ITER-1, keywords iter and yield). The reference evaluator runs the iterator with a yield cap, delivers values to the loop body, and re-runs with a doubled cap only when the body asks for more; gen_prefix shows this equals the push model. Lean: RCE/Iter.lean.
